title: The gift of silence
tomorrow: sunday langar dish duty. so why does bebe point at the sink?

cards: Lunch, Friday. Tara drops her tray at the next table, loud enough. So, fake nice, still saving everyone?
A few people laugh. Simran feels the old comeback loading, the one that would win. Maya's knee presses hers under the table.
Kiran is sitting with them now, for the first time in weeks, watching to see what she'll do. Simran opens her mouth. And then she doesn't.

teach.h: THE JAPJI: SILENCE ISN'T JUST QUIET.
teach.b: Here's the twist the Japji puts right at its start. By keeping silent, Guru Nanak says, silence doesn't come, even if you stay absorbed without a break. Outer quiet alone isn't the point.
So the gift of silence isn't the cold shoulder, and it isn't swallowing everything forever.
It's choosing not to feed a fire when speaking would only feed it. Simran's quiet lets Tara's line just sit there, with nothing to bounce off. After a beat, someone changes the subject.
And silence that serves can still speak later: after school, Simran tells Maya exactly how much it stung.

teach.h: A WEEK OF WORDS, LOOKED BACK ON.
teach.b: Now look back at the week, because this silence is made of all of it. No gossip: the joke never sent. True and kind: the text at midnight.
Listen fully: Kiran's mom. Sorry, plainly: one breath, no but. Where there is forgiveness: the deleted reply.
Kind online: the candle that never went up.
And now, a silence that serves.

how: Sikhs recite the Japji, whose first pauri says outer silence alone doesn't bring inner quiet; restraint in an argument is taught as part of humility, not as withdrawal.

games.q: what does “the gift of silence” mean?
o: choosing not to speak when words would hurt
refusing to talk to someone who upset you
staying quiet so nobody notices you at all

games.q: a week of words — tap the pairs.

s: the Japji praises keeping silent as the way to peace
its first pauri says silence doesn't come just by keeping silent.
the gift of silence can be choosing not to feed an argument
it's a choice, not a cold shoulder.

games.q: your sister keeps poking at you at dinner to start a fight. the comeback is perfect. what's the gift of silence here?
o: let the comeback go, and talk to her later, when it's calm.
give her the silent treatment for the rest of the week.
never bring it up; keeping quiet forever keeps the peace.
games.why: silence that serves isn't a punishment or a forever. it's not feeding the fire now, and speaking when words can help.

practice: Sit with your eyes closed and let the sounds around you come and go without answering any of them. When a reply to someone forms in your mind, let it stay unsaid. Notice what's left when nothing needs saying.

wordCard.voice: The gift of silence. Not the cold shoulder: the choice not to feed a fire. Chup is silence, in the Japji's first pauri.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chup, silence; the Japji's first pauri says outer silence alone doesn't bring it.

carryVoice: Your line: silence can serve. Not every quiet is empty; some of it is a gift. Rest well this weekend.

sources.ref: Japji, pauri 1 (Ang 1: chupai chup na hovaee je laae rahaa liv taar), paraphrased
